Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:10:1.english: When that [baraita] is taught - [the one stating] that he is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:10:2.hebrew: בחצר המיוחדת לזה ולזה - לפירות ולשוורים, דהויא ליה חצר השותפים לגבי שן ולגבי קרן. הלכך, בשן פטור ברה"ר, ובקרן תמה ח"נ ברה"ר משלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:10:2.english: In a courtyard designated for this [one] and for that [one] - For produce and for oxen, for it is [considered] a courtyard of partners with respect to Tooth [Eating] and with respect to Horn [Goring]. Therefore, for Tooth [Eating] he is exempt [as] in the public domain, and for an innocuous Horn he pays half-damages [as] in the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:10:3.hebrew: ודרב יוסף בחצר המיוחדת כו' - דהויא חצר הניזק, שלא היה לו להכניס שם שוורים, ולא דמי לרה"ר. פונדק אינו מיוחד לשוורים, לפי ששם מונחת פרגמטיא של סוחרים, ואינן מניחין ליכנס שם שוורים שלא ידחפו ויטנפו כליהם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:10:3.english: And [that] of Rav Yosef [was taught] regarding a courtyard designated, etc. - For it is [considered] the injured party's courtyard, since he had no right to bring oxen in there, and it is not similar to a public domain. An inn is not designated for oxen, because merchants' merchandise is placed there, and they do not allow oxen to enter there lest they push and soil their wares.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:10:4.english: An ordinary valley — oxen graze there.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:12:1.english: We require “a field of another,” and it is not [met] - For the damager has permission in it to bring in his produce.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:13:1.hebrew: שדה אחר קרינן ביה - שהרי נכנס שלא ברשות, שלא היה לו רשות לשוורים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:13:1.english: We call it “the field of another” - For behold, [the ox] entered without permission, since [its owner] did not have permission for oxen [to enter].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:14:1.hebrew: אמוראי נמי לא פליגי - דהא דרב חסדא בשאינה מיוחדת לשוורים, ודרבי אלעזר במיוחדת אף לשוורים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:14:1.english: The Amoraim also do not disagree - For that [statement] of Rav Chisda [refers to a property] that is not designated for oxen, and that of Rabbi Elazar [refers to one] that is designated even for oxen.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:15:1.hebrew: בקושיא דר' זירא ופירוקא דאביי - ובחצר המיוחדת לפירות ולא לשוורים. רב חסדא כאביי, דכיון דאינה מיוחדת לשוורים, שדה אחר קרינא ביה; ורבי אלעזר כרבי זירא, כיון דיש למזיק רשות בה לפירות, לא קרינא ביה שדה אחר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:15:1.english: In the difficulty of Rabbi Zeira and the resolution of Abaye - And [this is] in a courtyard designated for produce and not for oxen. Rav Chisda [holds] like Abaye, for since it is not designated for oxen, we call it "the field of another"; and Rabbi Elazar [holds] like Rabbi Zeira, [that] since the damager has permission in it for produce, we do not call it "the field of another."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:17:1.hebrew: חייב על הכל לא קתני - דליהוי משמע על השן והרגל ועל הקרן, אלא חייב בכל, דמשמע על הקרן, אע"ג שהוא תם, אתא לאשמועינן דחייב נ"ש:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:17:1.english: It does not teach "liable for everything" - So that it would imply for Tooth, Foot, and Horn; rather, [it teaches] "liable for all," which implies regarding Horn [that] even though it is innocuous, it comes to teach us that one is liable for full damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:18:1.english: It is Rabbi Tarfon, who says - Later, in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad (Bava Kamma 24b).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:18:2.hebrew: משונה קרן בחצר הניזק נ"ש משלם - קרן תמה וכל תולדותיה קרי משונה, הואיל ושינו את וסתן, שלא היו דרכן לכך:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:18:2.english: Atypical Horn in the courtyard of the injured party pays full damage - An innocuous Horn and all its derivatives [the Gemara] calls "atypical," since they changed their usual behavior, in that it was not their way [to act] thus.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:1:1.english: And he did not accept upon himself the safeguarding of its damages - if it damages others.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:20:1.hebrew: אלא דאחר - שאינו לא ניזק ולא מזיק, וקתני חייב על השן; והא בעינן שדה אחר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:20:1.english: Rather, [it belongs] to another - That [the field] is neither [the] injured party's nor [the] damager's, and [yet the baraita] teaches [that one is] liable for Tooth; but do we not require "a field of another"?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:21:1.english: Rather, [it belongs] to one of them - That is to say, to the injured party.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:24:1.hebrew: הא א"ל שמואל לרב יהודה כו' - לקמן גבי חמשה תמין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:24:1.english: Behold, Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda, etc. - Below, regarding [the Mishnah of] "Five [animals] are innocuous [tamim]."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:24:2.english: Leave the Mishnah - Do not trouble yourself to explain [it] according to a single Tanna.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:24:3.hebrew: ותא אבתראי - ואימא כוותי, דאוקי אנא רישא רבי טרפון וסיפא רבנן. וד' כללות דקאמר ר"ש, תרי מינייהו בחד דוכתא — חד כר' טרפון וחד כרבנן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:24:3.english: And follow after me - And say like me, for I establish the first clause [as] Rabbi Tarfon and the last clause [as] the Rabbis. And [regarding] the four general rules that Rabbi Shimon [ben Elazar] stated, two of them [are] in one place — one according to Rabbi Tarfon and one according to the Rabbis.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:25:1.english: Rather, [it is] of one - [i.e.,] of the injured party.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:26:1.hebrew: דלגבי שן הויא חצר הניזק - וחייב המזיק בנזקי שן, שהרי לגבי פירות אינה אלא דניזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:26:1.english: For with regard to Tooth, it is the courtyard of the injured party - And the damager is liable for Tooth damages, since with regard to produce, [the courtyard] belongs only to the injured party.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:26:2.hebrew: ולגבי קרן הויא רה"ר - שהרי ברשות הכניס שם שורו, ומשום הכי הוא משלם חצי נזק ותו לא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:26:2.english: And with regard to Horn, it is a public domain - For he brought his ox in there with permission, and therefore he pays half-damages and no more.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:27:1.hebrew: ג' כללות הוו - דהאי כללא בתרא שמעינן ליה מקמאי, דכיון דלגבי שן הויא חצר הניזק, למה ליה למתני "חייב על השן"? הא תנא ליה רישא: "כל שהוא רשות לניזק ולא למזיק — חייב בכל"! וקרן בחצר השותפין — הא תנא ליה רישא: "כגון חצר השותפין והבקעה, על הנגיחה ועל הנגיפה תם משלם חצי נזק":
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:27:1.english: There are three principles - For we learn this last principle from the earlier ones: since with respect to Tooth it is [considered] the courtyard of the injured party, why did [the Tanna] need to teach "he is liable for Tooth"? Behold, the first clause already taught: "Whatever is property of the injured party and not of the damager, he is liable for everything"! And [as for] Horn in a courtyard of partners — behold, the first clause already taught: "For example, a courtyard of partners and a valley: for goring and for pushing, an innocuous [animal] pays half-damages."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:4:1.english: Is that so? But didn't Rav Yosef teach - [The Gemara] raises an objection against Rabbi Elazar.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:4:2.hebrew: והפונדק - בית גדול שרגילין אורחים ואכסנאין ללון בו, ואם הזיק זה את זה, חייב אשן ורגל, ולא הוי כרה"ר, דהואיל ואינו מיוחד לבני רשות הרבים אלא לאותן הדרין בו, כשדה אחר קרינן ביה, שהרי ע"י שכירות הם דרים שם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:4:2.english: And an inn - A large house in which guests and lodgers are accustomed to stay overnight, and if one caused damage to another [there], he is liable for Tooth and Foot, and it is not [considered] like a public domain; for since it is not designated for the general public, [but] only for those who reside in it, we call it "another's field," since they reside there by way of rental.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:5:1.hebrew: ותסברא דמתניתא לא פליגי - דליכא ברייתא דקאי כוותי? והתניא, ד' כללות כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:5:1.english: And do you think that baraitot do not disagree - That there is no baraita that stands in accordance with my [view]? And was it not taught: Four principles, etc.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:5:2.hebrew: חייב בכל - לקמן מפרש שאפילו קרן תמה משלם נזק שלם, הואיל ונכנס לרשותו והזיקה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:5:2.english: Liable for all - Later on, [the Gemara] explains that even [for] an innocuous horn, he pays full damages, since it entered his [the injured party's] domain and caused damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:5:3.english: Exempt from all - For he says to him, "What business does your ox have in my property?"

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:6:1.hebrew: על השן ורגל - דלא קרינן ביה "בשדה אחר", דמשמע שיהא מיוחד לניזק. אבל על הנגיחה ועל הנגיפה והנשיכה והרביצה והבעיטה, שהן תולדותיו של קרן, תם משלם חצי נזק, דכרה"ר הוא, שהרי לשניהן רשות בו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:6:1.english: For Tooth and Foot - [One is exempt] because we do not apply to it [the verse] "in another's field," which implies that it must be designated exclusively for the injured party. However, for goring, and for pushing, biting, crouching, and kicking, which are subcategories of Horn, an innocuous [ox] pays half-damages, for it is like a public domain, since both of them have permission [to be] in it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:7:1.hebrew: לא לזה ולא לזה - מפרש לקמיה דאינו של שניהן, אלא של אחד מהן — של ניזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:7:1.english: Of neither this [one] nor that [one] - [The Gemara] explains further on that it is not [the property] of both of them, rather of one of them — of the injured party.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:7:2.hebrew: חייב בה על השן ועל הרגל - נ"ש:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:7:2.english: He is liable in it for Tooth and for Foot - [He pays] full damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:7:3.hebrew: ועל הנגיחה כו' - ולקמן פריך, הא תנא רישא דבחצר הניזק אפילו קרן תמה משלם נ"ש:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:7:3.english: And for goring, etc. - And later [the Gemara] asks: Behold, the first clause taught that in the courtyard of the injured party, even an innocuous horn pays full damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:8:1.hebrew: פטור בה על השן ועל הרגל - והיינו כר' אלעזר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:8:1.english: He is exempt in it for Tooth and for Foot - And this is in accordance with [the opinion of] Rabbi Elazar.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 14a:9:1.english: And the Gemara asks - [They] contradict one another.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 14a:1:1.hebrew: ולא קבל עליה שמירת נזקיו - ואם תאמר: כיון דלא קביל עליה, פשיטא דתם משלם חצי נזק ומועד משלם נזק שלם! ויש לומר: דסלקא דעתך דשמירת נזקין דעלמא לא קביל, אבל אנזקין לתורא דשואל גופיה סלקא דעתך שקבל, וליפטר משאיל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 14a:1:1.english: "And he did not undertake safeguarding it from causing damage" - And if you ask: Since he did not undertake [this responsibility], it is obvious that [if it is] a tam [an innocuous ox], he pays half-damage, and [if it is] a muad [a forewarned ox], he pays full damage! One can answer: It might have entered your mind that he did not undertake safeguarding against general damages [to others], but regarding damages to the borrower's own ox, it might have entered your mind that he did undertake [it], and [thus] the lender would be exempt.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 14a:25:1.hebrew: לא לזה ולא לזה לפירות אלא לחד - ר"ת גריס: "לא לזה ולא לזה לשוורים", דגבי שן הויא חצר הניזק שהזיק פירות, אבל גבי שוורים ה"ל קרן ברה"ר, כיון שלא היה להם רשות ליכנס. ול"ג כמו שכתוב בספרים "ולזה ולזה לשוורים", דא"כ גבי שן לא היה לו ליחשב חצר הניזק, כיון שיש רשות לכל חד וחד להכניס שם שורו, כדמוכח לעיל. ולא בעי לאוקמא "לזה ולזה לפירות ולא לשוורים", דלא כר' זירא, ועוד דלישנא לא משמע הכי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 14a:25:1.english: Neither to this one nor to that one for produce, rather to one [of them] - Rabbeinu Tam reads: "Neither to this one nor to that one for oxen" — for with regard to shen [Eating], it is [considered] the courtyard of the injured party, since [the animal] damaged produce [there]; whereas with regard to oxen, it is [considered] keren [Goring] in the public domain, since they did not have permission to enter [with their oxen]. And we do not read as is written in the books, "and to this one and to that one for oxen," for if so, with regard to shen it should not be considered the courtyard of the injured party, since each and every one has permission to bring his ox in there, as was proven above. And [the Gemara] did not want to establish [the baraita] as [referring to a courtyard belonging] "to this one and to that one for produce, and not for oxen," [because that would be] contrary to Rabbi Zeira, and furthermore, because the wording [of the baraita] does not imply this.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 14a:27:1.hebrew: אי הכי ארבעה שלשה הוו - בשלמא לשמואל דמוקי רישא רבי טרפון וסיפא רבנן, אצטריך סיפא לאשמועינן לאפוקי מדרבי טרפון; אלא לרבינא לא צריכא כלל, דלגבי שן הוי חצר הניזק — שמעינן מכל שהוא רשות לניזק, וקרן ברה"ר — שמעינן מחצר השותפין והבקעה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 14a:27:1.english: If that is so, [does the baraita list] four [principles]? There are [only] three! - It is well according to Shmuel, who establishes the first clause [in accordance with] Rabbi Tarfon and the latter clause [in accordance with] the Rabbis — the latter clause is necessary to teach us [this] so as to exclude [the view] of Rabbi Tarfon. However, according to Ravina, it is not needed at all: for [that] with respect to Tooth it is [considered] the courtyard of the injured party, we learn from "[any place] that is a domain for the injured party"; and [that for] Horn [it is considered] a public domain, we learn from "a courtyard of partners and a valley."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 14a:5:1.hebrew: מי לא פליגי - הוי מצי לאוקמי ההיא דרב יוסף לא לזה ולא לזה לשוורים, ולפירות דחד:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 14a:5:1.english: Are there not [baraitot] that disagree? - [The Gemara] could have established that [baraita] of Rav Yosef [as referring to a courtyard designated] neither for this one nor for that one for oxen, and for the produce of one [of them].
